description: One placed object in a room's object list (gLevelObjLists[objectListIdx]->unk0, see object_lists.json). The list is walked by stride (unk1) until a zero stride. The header fields below have one meaning for every type; from subtype1 on, fields are per-type parameters documented in object_params.json (the descriptions here give only the generic part).
notes: 3,482 records in 287 lists (longest 30); every retail record is 36 bytes with spawnTable 1 and unkA/unkB/unkD = 0xFF.

Spawning: CreateLevelObjects and the two scroll-in walks (game/src/code_080023A4.c ~5914-6014) skip an object whose despawn flag (unk2, unk3) is set, and, unless unk5 bit 0 is set, objects outside the spawn window around the viewport; CreateObject then calls gSpawnFuncTable{spawnTable}[type](template, playerId).
Positions: x/y are pixels, InitObject turns them into 8.8 world coordinates; object placement is free (not cell-snapped), though most retail values are multiples of 8.

fields.name: spawnTable
fields.description: Which constructor table type indexes: 1 = gSpawnFuncTable1 (all retail data), 2 = gSpawnFuncTable2 (never selected by level data).

2.name: table2
2.description: reachable only from code; untested by retail levels

fields.name: size
fields.description: Byte stride to the next record; 0 terminates the list. Always 36 in retail data, but the walker honours any value, so a record may carry extra trailing bytes.

fields.name: despawnScope
fields.description: Which 'already collected / defeated' bitmap unk3 indexes. If the bit is set the object is not spawned. 0 = per room visit (cleared on every room load, 32 bits), 1 = per area (cleared on area change, warp star and some Kirby transitions; used by all food/battery/1UP pickups so they stay collected while you remain in the area), 2 = saved with the file (never used by level data).

evidence.code: u32 sub_080027E8(u32 arg0, u16 arg1, u8 arg2)

evidence.data: 0 in 3,077 records (unk3 0..28), 1 in 399 (unk3 0..255; exactly the consumables), 2 in none

fields.name: despawnBit
fields.description: Bit index in the bitmap chosen by unk2; the object's constructor/defeat code sets it (sub_08001678) so it does not respawn. Must be unique per room (scope 0) or per area (scope 1). (unk2 = 0, unk3 = 31) is the 'no flag' sentinel used by dynamically created objects; level data never uses it, and the defeat counter (unk4) skips objects that carry it.

evidence.data: no room has two objects with the same (unk2, unk3); scope-1 ids form contiguous per-area blocks

fields.name: roomRegister
fields.description: Index of a per-room-visit u32 counter (GetStateSlot(STATE_SLOT_ROOM, unk4), 16 per room slot, zeroed at room load). Defeating an enemy increments its register; gates such as sliding doors, lava walls, scroll locks, Jack, big buttons watch theirs. 0 = none by convention. This is the 'beat all the enemies to open the wall' mechanism, entirely data-driven. Some types reinterpret it (see object_params.json).

evidence.data: non-zero on scroll locks, buttons, sliding doors, bosses, cannons, doors-to-hub; room 801's hub mirrors use up to 18 (beyond the 16 room registers: they are read as another scope, see object_params)

fields.name: spawnFlags
fields.description: Spawn behaviour bits.

bits.name: spawnAtLoad
bits.description: Create the object when the room loads regardless of the camera (skip the viewport proximity test). Used by camera controllers, room logic and every boss.

evidence.data: 235/3,476 records have it, all controllers, gates and bosses

fields.name: x
fields.description: Object x in room pixels (InitObject: base.x = x * 0x100).

fields.name: y
fields.description: Object y in room pixels (y grows downward in room space).
No reader found; 0xFF in every record. Preserve.
No reader found; 0xFF in every record. Preserve.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Object type (game/include/constants/object_types.h): selects the constructor and the obj_desc descriptor (HP, ability, palette, tile budget).
No reader found; 0xFF in every record (likely padding after type). Preserve.

fields.name: variant
fields.description: Per-type behaviour / appearance variant (movement pattern for enemies, contents for chests, ability slot for statues, door art, warp-star route ...). Its enum is private to each type: see object_params.json.

evidence.note: every consumer is a switch inside one type's constructor

evidence.data: 27+ distinct values, small consistent sets per type

fields.name: paletteVariant
fields.description: Sprite palette variant passed with the type's palette id to sub_0803DFAC (every other caller passes 0). Mostly 0; non-zero on chests, doors-to-hub, triggerable walls.

fields.name: subtype
fields.description: Copied to the runtime object's subtype by InitObject; meaning per type (often facing or a secondary variant): see object_params.json.

fields.name: param11
fields.description: Per-type parameter (chest id, button register value, CPU-trigger route rank, ...).

evidence.note: no generic reader; every consumer is one type

fields.name: param12
fields.description: Per-type parameter (scroll-lock window size, spawner interval, cannon timing, ...).

fields.name: param14
fields.description: Per-type parameter (scroll-lock anchor, spawned type, big-button effect, cannon direction, ...).

fields.name: param16
fields.description: Per-type parameter; non-zero only on 5 flame columns in retail data.

fields.name: param18
fields.description: Per-type parameter (spawner progress threshold, button timer, ...).

fields.name: rectX
fields.description: Left edge of a region relative to the object's x (trigger volume, arena, travel extent). Used by many types with the same decomposition; meaning of the region is per type.

fields.name: rectY
fields.description: Top edge of the region relative to the object's y.

evidence.data: boss arenas carry e.g. (-176, -48, 256, 136): a screen-sized box around the boss

fields.name: rectW
fields.description: Region width (some types reuse the slot, e.g. warp stars/shards: destination room id).

fields.name: rectH
fields.description: Region height.

fields.name: flags
fields.description: Per-type bitfield (chest facing, door marker art, scroll-lock mode, spawner trigger mode, ...). No cross-type meaning: see object_params.json.

evidence.note: bit 0 means different things in chest.c, object_spawner.c, scroll_lock.c
